# kbcli v0.3.1

**Release date:** 2026-11-22 · **Previous release:** [v0.3.0](https://github.com/ProjAnvil/kbcli/releases/tag/v0.3.0) · **License:** MIT · **Go:** 1.27.4

A patch release that corrects a silent retrieval-quality defect in the neural
embedder, makes hybrid retrieval the default, and gives the project its first
repeatable retrieval measurement. It keeps the single-binary, zero-cgo design:
no new dependency, no change to binary size, and no model weight embedded in
the executable.

> **Heads up:** if you use `embedder: rembed`, rebuild the index once with
> `kbcli reindex`. The old symmetric-prefix vectors are incompatible and the
> loader now rejects them. The default `local` embedder needs no action.

See the [full diff](https://github.com/ProjAnvil/kbcli/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1)
and [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ProjAnvil/kbcli/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete entry.

---

## Highlights

- **Correct e5 prefixes.** The `rembed` provider embedded queries and
  documents with the same `"query: "` prefix. e5 models require `"query: "` on
  queries and `"passage: "` on documents. The mismatch does not raise an
  error; it quietly lowers recall. Queries and documents now take separate
  prefixes through an optional `QueryPrefixer` capability.
- **Hybrid retrieval by default.** `retrieval_method` now defaults to
  `hybrid`. Dense vectors and BM25 are fused with weighted RRF before
  reranking, so exact identifiers, version strings and Chinese terms are no
  longer lost to a vector-only first stage. This is a query-time default and
  needs no rebuild for `local` indexes.
- **`kbcli eval`.** A deterministic self-retrieval smoke test over indexed
  chunks. Reports `recall@1`, `recall@k`, MRR and p50/p95 latency with no API
  key, no labelled data and no model download. Designed for CI regression
  checks.
- **`kbcli search --json`.** A stable JSON shape for tool consumers, with
  `rank`, `score`, `source`, `heading`, `body` and `id`.
- **Smaller neural footprint.** `rembed.Load` now uses weight-only int8
  quantization: about 4x less weight traffic with cosine >= 0.999 against
  fp32.

---

## What's Changed

### Fixes

- `internal/embed/prefix.go`: new `QueryPrefixer` capability plus
  `EmbedQuery`, `EmbedDocuments` and `DocumentText`. Providers without the
  capability keep using text unchanged, so the default hashing embedder is
  bit-for-bit compatible.
- `internal/embed/rembed.go`: `EmbedBatch` no longer prepends a prefix.
  `CountForEmbedding` counts the document-side prefix. `rembedVersion` now
  appends `#v2` so `loadStore` rejects old `.kbvec` files instead of
  comparing incompatible vectors.
- `internal/index/store.go` and `internal/index/search.go`: indexing goes
  through `EmbedDocuments`, searching through `EmbedQuery`.
- `internal/config/config.go`: `IndexSignature()` records `embed_domain` for
  `rembed` only, so `local` indexes keep their existing signature.
  `IndexSignatureChanges` now reports every differing key, including derived
  keys such as `chunker` and `embed_domain` that have no editable setting.
- `internal/config/config.go`: `rembed.Load(ref, rembed.WithInt8())`. rembed
  falls back to fp32 on CPUs without AVX2+FMA.

### Defaults

- `retrieval_method`: `vector` -> `hybrid`. Restore the previous behaviour
  with `kbcli config set retrieval_method vector`.
- No setting was added or removed. The catalog remains 49 fields in 7 groups.

### Features

- `internal/cli/eval.go`: `kbcli eval [--samples N] [--top-k K] [--json]`.
  Queries are a trimmed prefix of chunk bodies, sampled at a fixed stride so
  repeated runs use the same set. Recall is optimistic by design; use the
  command to compare configurations, not to claim absolute answer quality.
- `internal/cli/search.go`: `--json` prints a stable array of hits. The human
  readable output is unchanged.
- `internal/app/app.go`: `App.Chunks()` exposes a defensive chunk snapshot for
  the evaluation command.

### Tests

- `internal/embed/prefix_test.go`: plain and asymmetric stub embedders, e5
  prefix values, and the domain version.
- `internal/index/prefix_test.go`: end-to-end assertion that `Add` encodes
  with `passage: ` and `Search` encodes with `query: `.
- `internal/embed/provider_test.go`, `internal/settings/settings_test.go` and
  `internal/tui/settings_test.go`: expectations updated for the new version
  key and the new retrieval default.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test -race -count=1 ./...` pass on
  all 16 packages.

---

## Breaking Changes

- **`rembed` indexes are invalidated.** The embedder domain version changed
  from `rembed:<ref>` to `rembed:<ref>#v2`. `loadStore` rejects a file whose
  `EmbedderVersion` differs and asks for `kbcli reindex`. No compatibility
  shim is provided. This affects only users who set `embedder: rembed`.
- **Default retrieval changed.** Queries now run BM25 plus dense vectors with
  RRF fusion. Result ranking, `min_score` behaviour on the fused scores and
  query latency can differ. Set `retrieval_method: vector` to restore the
  v0.3.0 behaviour.
- **BM25 index construction is now on the default path.** The first query
  after startup builds the in-memory BM25 snapshot from the chunk set. It is
  cached and rebuilt only when the store revision changes.
- **Neural weight quantization.** `rembed` now loads int8 weights. Vectors
  differ slightly from fp32, which is another reason the old index must be
  rebuilt.

---

## Upgrade Guide

1. **Install v0.3.1** (see [Installation](#installation)).
2. **If you use `embedder: rembed`, rebuild once.** Run `kbcli reindex` in the
   workspace, or type `:reindex` inside the TUI. The old `.kbvec` stays on
   disk and is ignored.
3. **If you use the default `local` embedder, do nothing.** Its vectors,
   version (`local-v1`) and build signature are unchanged.
4. **Establish a baseline.** Run `kbcli eval --samples 50` and record
   `recall@1`, `recall@k` and `mrr` before changing retrieval settings.
5. **Compare retrieval modes.** `kbcli config set retrieval_method vector`
   followed by another `kbcli eval` shows what hybrid adds on your corpus.
   Restore `hybrid` when done.
6. **Tune if needed.** `hybrid_vector_weight` controls the RRF weight of the
   vector list; BM25 receives `1 - w`. `bm25_top_k` controls the sparse
   candidate pool.

## Installation

### From source

```sh
go install github.com/ProjAnvil/kbcli/cmd/kbcli@v0.3.1
# or
go install github.com/ProjAnvil/kbcli/cmd/kbcli@latest
```

Requires Go 1.27.4 or newer. `make install` also works from a checkout and
stamps the binary with `git describe --tags`.

### Prebuilt binaries

Each release publishes two tiers per platform. Asset names carry the OS and
architecture; full-tier names also contain `full`.

| Tier | Asset name | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | `kbcli-v0.3.1-darwin-arm64` | Binary only; the reranker model downloads on first run. |
| Full | `kbcli-full-v0.3.1-darwin-arm64.tar.gz` | Binary plus `model/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2/`; fully offline. |

Platforms: `darwin-amd64`, `darwin-arm64`, `linux-amd64`, `linux-arm64`,
`windows-amd64`. Windows full tier ships as a `.zip`.

```sh
tar -xzf kbcli-full-v0.3.1-darwin-arm64.tar.gz
./kbcli
```

### Verify downloads

```sh
# macOS: shasum -a 256 -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing
# Linux: sha256sum -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing
kbcli version
kbcli config get retrieval_method   # hybrid
kbcli eval --samples 20             # no API key required
```

---

## Known Issues

- The default `local` embedder is still a zero-dependency hashing model. It
  remains the largest recall bottleneck; `embedder: rembed` is opt-in.
- `rembed` int8 weight quantization falls back to fp32 on CPUs without
  AVX2+FMA. Vectors can then differ slightly across machines. Rebuild a
  `.kbvec` on a host with a different CPU feature set when exact
  reproducibility matters.
- The vector width is fixed at 384. Models with 768 or 1024 dimensions are
  not usable yet.
- `chunk_size: 4000` is a rune cap, while the default neural model accepts
  about 512 tokens. `capPassagesByTokens` hard-splits over-long sections, so
  the rune cap has little effect for `rembed` users.
- `Chunk.Metadata` is never populated and retrieval has no metadata filter.
- `kbcli eval` is a self-retrieval smoke test, not a question-answer
  benchmark. Queries come from chunk bodies, so recall is optimistic.
- Retrieval still uses an exact brute-force scan with a full sort. An ANN
  index and vector quantization are not implemented.
- `read_file` can read any text file inside the workspace, including `.env`
  style secrets. Its results are not numbered with `[n]`.
- The boot and reindex full-screen modals still accept only `ctrl+c`.
- `direct` (greeting / smalltalk) answers are still returned in one shot.
- Windows runtime behavior has not been verified on real hardware. Only
  cross-compilation and static checks were performed.
